name: Dharwad
headline: A rural Dharwad study ties dropout to hardship and migration; child marriage is also being stopped.
summary: A study of rural Dharwad attributes high upper-primary and early-secondary dropout to disinterest, economic hardship and families migrating for wage work. The district's SSLC rank rose while its pass percentage fell, which The Hindu reported but did not link to dropout. Authorities prevented 28 child marriages in 2024-25 and launched Mission Vidyakashi to improve SSLC and PU results.

reasons.detail: A study of Dharwad's rural areas found dropouts driven by student disinterest, economic hardship and families moving for wage labour.
Officials stopped 28 child marriages in 2024-25, evidence of ongoing pressure to marry girls out of school.
Many of the roughly 150 unenrolled children in 2025 belong to migrant families working in agricultural fields with parents, or have moved out of the district.
Some children never attended school; others obtained transfer certificates but were not admitted elsewhere, pointing to gaps in tracking and re-enrolment after movement.
Dharwad moved up the SSLC ranking while its pass percentage fell; the report reads this as weaker students leaving, which the sources do not confirm.
Ten children were rescued from labour in Hubballi-Dharwad during a September 2026 statewide police drive; the report does not say whether they were school dropouts.
A 2015 NGO drive proposed an attendance authority to act when a child is absent a week without reason, indicating irregular attendance preceded dropout.
A 2015 geographical study of Dharwad district reported that dropout rates were increasing and examined causes and effects; the abstract gives no specific figures or causes.

responses.text: Mission Vidyakashi aims to improve teaching methods and SSLC and PU results.

After the 2025 survey, the list was sent to the education department; the DDPI promised taluk-level outreach, while cluster resource persons and school heads will visit households to reintegrate children.
Returning first-time students are to be placed in age-appropriate classes under the reintegration plan announced in May 2025.
